researcher_notes: Existing current_ref (NS Energy) is live and states the CO2/carbon-dioxide nature of the line ('captured and processed up to 45 million cubic feet of CO2 ... transported through an 80km-long pipeline'). Added two independent corroborators: OGJ ('injection of 40 MMscfd of carbon dioxide ... piped 85 km to Uthmaniyah field') and MIT Sequestration project page. 3 independent sources all confirm the transported fluid is CO2 (carbon dioxide). High confidence.

current_ref (NS Energy) is live and describes a dedicated point-to-point CO2 trunk line carrying captured CO2 ~80 km from the Hawiyah capture facility to the Uthmaniyah injection field. No source uses the literal word 'transmission' — 'transmission' is a GEM PipelineType classification inferred from the function (a long-distance trunk line between a source plant and an injection field, not gathering/distribution). The classification is reasonable but not verbatim-sourced, so REVERIFIED at medium rather than high. Keeping the live current_ref; no value change recommended.

Operating status corroborated by 3 independent sources: NS Energy ('Completed in 2015'), SCCS Edinburgh ('Operation formally launched July 2015'), and MIT Sequestration ('Operational 2015'). The Uthmaniyah CO2-EOR demonstration project has been injecting CO2 continuously since July 2015 — operating is well supported. High confidence.

Start year 2015 corroborated by 3 independent sources: SCCS Edinburgh specifies 'Operation formally launched July 2015' (so StartMonth could be added as 7), NS Energy 'Completed in 2015', MIT 'Operational 2015'. CO2 injection began July 2015. High confidence on the 2015 start year.

GEM value is 80 km. The current_ref (NS Energy) is live and states exactly '80km-long pipeline' — so the existing ref supports the value. HOWEVER independent sources DISAGREE on the length: OGJ, MIT Sequestration, CSLF and Saudipedia all give 85 km ('piped 85 km to Uthmaniyah field'), while SCCS Edinburgh gives ~70 km. Only NS Energy matches 80 km exactly. Because the only source matching the GEM 80 km value is the single existing ref and the independent corroborators point to 85 km, this is REVERIFIED at medium (single-source for the exact figure) — NOT high. Possible GEM divergence: the more commonly cited figure is 85 km. Flagging for Update review; not overwriting. Keeping the live current_ref.

FuelSource = 'Ghawar oil & gas Field'. The CO2 is captured at the Hawiyah (NGL) gas plant, which Saudipedia explicitly states 'is considered part of the Ghawar Field' and which processes Ghawar-complex gas before pumping the captured CO2 ~85 km to the Uthmaniyah oilfield. NS Energy also ties the CO2 capture to the Ghawar field operation. So 'Ghawar oil & gas Field' is defensible as the broad fuel/CO2 source (Hawiyah is a production area of the greater Ghawar field). NOTE / precision nuance: the specific capture facility is the Hawiyah NGL recovery plant; if GEM wants the immediate source it would be 'Hawiyah NGL plant (Ghawar field)'. Two independent sources tie the source to Ghawar; medium tier because the value names the field rather than the exact capture plant. Not overwriting; flagging the Hawiyah nuance for Update.

StartLocation = 'Al Hasa', Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. The pipeline start (CO2 capture point) is the Hawiyah gas/NGL plant. SCCS Edinburgh places the project 'Near Al Hofuf, Eastern Province' — Al Hofuf is the capital of the Al-Ahsa (Al Hasa) Governorate, supporting 'Al Hasa, Eastern Province'. CONFLICT: a Saudipedia article instead locates a Hawiyah gas plant in Al-Jubail Industrial City (Eastern Province), so the exact governorate of the capture facility is not cleanly settled across sources. Eastern Province / Saudi Arabia are solidly confirmed; the 'Al Hasa' district sits on one source (SCCS, via Al Hofuf) with a conflicting alternative — hence LOW tier. Could not reach 2 fully independent sources agreeing on 'Al Hasa' as the start district. Flagging the location conflict for Update; not overwriting.

EndLocation = 'Uthmaniyah' (injection field), Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. Strongly corroborated by 3 independent sources: OGJ ('piped 85 km to Uthmaniyah field'), NS Energy ('injection into the reservoir of the Uthmaniyah oil field'), and MIT Sequestration (Uthmaniyah injection site). Uthmaniyah is a production unit of the greater Ghawar field in the Eastern Province. High confidence.
